clue.text: Scope for firm with a thousand to spend

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to pass time is to spend it

explanation.surface: A business allowed to spend a thousand pounds is being given room to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean range or extent, as in the compass of a voice, so it is a synonym of scope.

clue.text: A bit of a wag, even a joker maybe

definitions.meaning: a wag is a witty, amusing person, a bit of a character
a joker is one example of a playing ...

explanation.surface: Someone who is something of a comedian, even a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: Card is old slang for an eccentric, amusing person, and the joker is a playing card.

clue.text: An everyday conclusion, say, in film

parts.note: every day ends at twelve o'clock at night
to express something is to say it

explanation.surface: A film about ordinary endings, spoken of in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Express is a 1978 Alan Parker prison film, so the answer is a film title.

clue.text: Get off for a match

definitions.meaning: to get off a bus or train is to step down from it
a match is something you give someone to light up with

explanation.surface: Getting down from a train to fetch a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Alight means dismount from a vehicle, and a light, said as one word, is a match offered to a smoker.

clue.text: Grow something to eat

definitions.meaning: to grow is to put out shoots

explanation.surface: Growing your own food.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout is to begin growing, and sprouts are small cabbage-like vegetables eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Conceited boss?

parts.note: a slang name for an important person or boss, which also describes someone with an inflated opinion of themselves

explanation.surface: A complaint about a manager full of their own importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen-headed person is vain, and a 'big head' is also jocular slang for someone in charge.

clue.text: Inferior position of some driving instructors

definitions.text: Inferior position of some driving instructors

parts.words: Inferior position of some driving instructors
parts.note: a subordinate role, read as where unwanted advisers sit telling the driver what to do

explanation.surface: The humble place from which certain driving teachers give orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a back seat is to accept a lesser role, and back-seat drivers give unwanted instructions from behind.

clue.text: Father uncouth teenager

indicators.note: uncouth suggests rough and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dad whose teenager is loutish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncouth' rearranges TEENAGER. 'Father' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To father is to beget or produce offspring, so it means to bring into being.

clue.text: Perpetual figure in matrimonial disputes?

parts.note: an everlasting geometric shape, read as the love triangle behind many marital rows

explanation.surface: Someone who always turns up in rows between married couples.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a relationship of three people involving infidelity, a classic cause of marital strife.

clue.text: Attribute of the successful gear selector

definitions.text: Attribute of the successful gear selector

parts.words: Attribute of the successful gear selector
parts.note: suggests driving skill with gears, but gear here means clothing

explanation.surface: A quality that makes someone good at changing gear in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means good taste in clothes, and clothes are informally called gear.

clue.text: They meet in the centre of the ring

definitions.text: They meet in the centre of the ring

parts.words: They meet in the centre of the ring
parts.note: reads like boxers meeting mid-ring, but describes the lines from a circle's edge that converge at its middle

explanation.surface: Two boxers square up in the middle of the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry the lines from circumference to centre all join at the circle's middle point.

clue.text: Scattered once and never to get together again

indicators.note: scattered letters are spread about and regathered in a new order

explanation.surface: A group that broke up for good, with no reunion in prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered' rearranges ONCE and NEVER together; 'and' and 'to' are links. The surface says never meeting again, the answer means meeting again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble once more after a break, a direct synonym of meeting again.

clue.text: A brass band plays so freely

definitions.meaning: a brass band has no violins or other bowed instruments in it
given with no conditions attached, as a gift with no obligations

explanation.surface: Musicians in a brass band playing with abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a gift with no conditions matches 'freely'; a brass band literally lacks a string section.

clue.text: Pack with no score in even game

parts.note: a deck is a pack of cards

indicators.note: one piece is put in the middle of the other

parts.note: quits means even, with nothing owed
O is zero, a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A card pack and a scoreless draw in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside QUITS to make QUOITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck quoits is a ring-tossing game played on board ships.

clue.text: Repeat after some reflection

parts.note: sounds like repeating something after thinking it over, but means a sound bounced back off a surface

explanation.surface: Saying something again once you have thought about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is a sound repeated after bouncing off a wall or cliff, which is reflection of sound.

clue.text: Safe in sordid foreign jail

indicators.note: one word is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: base means low and sordid
a till is a cash drawer, a kind of safe for money

explanation.surface: A strongbox found inside a squalid prison abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective but is a noun, the cash drawer of a shop; 'in' puts it inside the word for sordid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789, so a jail in France.

clue.text: Lion and mule in scuffle on the floor

indicators.note: animals in a scuffle are tumbled about, so the letters mix

explanation.surface: A lion and a mule fighting on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in scuffle' rearranges LION and MULE; 'and' joins them and 'on the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum is a hard-wearing floor covering, so it stands for the floor itself.

clue.text: Grave commitments for NUR and ASLEF combined

indicators.note: the two union names are combined and stirred together

explanation.surface: Serious undertakings agreed by two British rail unions acting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combined' rearranges NUR and ASLEF, the former National Union of Railwaymen and the train drivers' union. 'Grave' looks like serious but means burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Funerals commit the dead to the grave, a pun on serious commitments.

clue.text: Don't slacken when flying a kite?

definitions.text: Don't slacken when flying a kite?

parts.words: Don't slacken when flying a kite?
parts.note: an encouragement to carry on, read literally as keeping the kite aloft

explanation.surface: Advice to a kite-flyer not to let the line go slack.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means continue the good work, and literally a kite-flyer must hold the kite aloft.

clue.text: Recklessly risk one's arm in Malaya?

indicators.note: done recklessly, the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in Malaya rashly risking a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recklessly' rearranges RISK. 'Arm' looks like a limb but means a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The kris is the traditional wavy-bladed dagger of Malaya, a weapon or arm.

clue.text: Come up with trial bearing on African fly

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a test is a trial
SE, south-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Emerging with an experimental result about an African insect.
explanation.walkthrough: TEST turned upward by 'Come up' gives TSET; 'with' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is a blood-sucking African fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: A shapeless mass — something with which one may play and work

parts.words: something with which one may play
parts.note: a doll is a toy to play with
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A formless lump of clay, a toy and a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump of something soft, such as cream.

clue.text: The amateur plainness of our production

indicators.note: a production of these words is a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A review sneering at the plain, amateurish staging of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges all fourteen letters of PLAINNESS OF OUR; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprofessional describes work done in a non-expert, amateurish way, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Lake in rising resort in the mountains

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the other
in a down clue, rising means read upward, so backwards

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A lake beside a resort high among mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: L inside SPA gives SPLA; 'rising' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great European mountain range, so they are the mountains.

clue.text: "Get in lane" order unfinished

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A driver's instruction to change lanes, left half-said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges GET IN LANE. 'unfinished' means lacking polish here, not left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelegant is unrefined or lacks finish, as unpolished or unfinished work does.

clue.text: It's perfectly right, for example, inside — all wrong outside

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit outside, around the other piece
set wrong, the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Something is fully correct when the example inside is right even if everything around it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns ALL into LAL; both 'inside' and 'outside' point the same way, the example sitting within the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means permitted by law, entirely right and proper.

clue.text: Understands mother's cutting back plants

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the middle of the other

parts.note: sees means understands, as in I see

indicators.note: reading back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: MA is mother, with the 's kept as S

explanation.surface: A mother pruning plants she understands well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MA'S into SAM; 'cutting' looks like pruning in the garden surface but means going into the middle of the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is an oilseed crop, so these are examples of plants.

clue.text: Printer's measure newspapers with ruler

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in typesetting
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A printer measuring newspaper columns with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female emperor, a sovereign ruler.
